coreShorts.q: Define dermatology.
coreShorts.a: The field of medicine dealing with diagnosis and treatment of skin disorders.

coreShorts.q: How important is skin in body size and weight?
coreShorts.a: Skin is the largest organ; the lecture states approximately 1/7 of total body weight and an average adult surface area of 1.75 m².

coreShorts.q: Which structures are examined in a general dermatological examination?
coreShorts.a: Skin, hair, nails and mucous membranes.

coreShorts.q: Which systemic problem is linked with pallor?
coreShorts.a: Anemia.

coreShorts.q: Which systemic problem is linked with cyanosis?
coreShorts.a: Hypoxia (the lecture mentions COPD as an example).

coreShorts.q: Which systemic disease does the lecture link with jaundice?
coreShorts.a: Hepatitis.

coreShorts.q: Which two skin diseases can be associated with thyroid disease?
coreShorts.a: Vitiligo and alopecia areata.

coreShorts.q: Which infection may be suggested by lichen planus?
coreShorts.a: Hepatitis C.

coreShorts.q: What is the outermost skin layer?
coreShorts.a: Epidermis; it rests on the basement membrane.

coreShorts.q: Name three epidermal cell types.
coreShorts.a: Keratinocytes, melanocytes and Langerhans cells.

coreShorts.q: Which epidermal cells produce keratin?
coreShorts.a: Keratinocytes, the main cells of the epidermis.

coreShorts.q: What is the order of the four epidermal cell layers from deep to superficial?
coreShorts.a: Basal → prickle (squamous) → granular → horny (stratum corneum).

coreShorts.q: Which layer renews the epidermis through active cell division?
coreShorts.a: Basal cell layer; it rests on the basement membrane.

coreShorts.q: Which epidermal layer contains keratohyaline granules?
coreShorts.a: Granular cell layer.

coreShorts.q: Describe the cells in the horny layer.
coreShorts.a: Dead keratinocytes without nuclei; it is the outermost layer.

coreShorts.q: What is the role of melanocytes and Langerhans cells?
coreShorts.a: Melanocytes synthesize melanin contributing to skin colour; Langerhans cells contribute to skin immune function.

coreShorts.q: Where is the dermis and what are its main matrix components?
coreShorts.a: Below the basement membrane; contains collagen fibres, elastic fibres and glycosaminoglycan matrix.

coreShorts.q: What structures are present in the dermis?
coreShorts.a: Blood vessels, lymphatics, nerve fibres/endings, hair follicles, sebaceous glands and sweat glands.

coreShorts.q: Describe the hypodermis.
coreShorts.a: Subcutaneous tissue with lobules of fat cells separated by fibrous septa containing collagen and large blood vessels.

coreShorts.q: What structural protein is emphasised for nails and hair shafts?
coreShorts.a: Hard keratin.

coreShorts.q: What happens to sebum in the sebaceous glands?
coreShorts.a: Sebum is discharged into hair follicles, assisted by the action of arrector pili muscles.

coreShorts.q: Where do eccrine sweat glands open?
coreShorts.a: On the epidermal surface through sweat ducts distributed over the body surface.

coreShorts.q: Where do apocrine sweat glands discharge and where are they present?
coreShorts.a: Into pilosebaceous ducts; in flexures, areolae, genitalia and eyelids.

coreShorts.q: List the protective roles of skin.
coreShorts.a: Protection against physical injury, thermal injury, invading microorganisms and ultraviolet rays; also prevents water and electrolyte loss.

coreShorts.q: How does skin regulate temperature?
coreShorts.a: Vasodilatation, vasoconstriction and evaporation of sweat.

coreShorts.q: Name the four sensations listed in the lecture.
coreShorts.a: Temperature, pain, pressure and touch.

coreShorts.q: What vitamin-related function of skin is listed?
coreShorts.a: Formation of vitamin D from its precursor under UVB in sunlight.

coreShorts.q: Which cells participate in skin immunological function?
coreShorts.a: Dendritic cells, keratinocytes and lymphocytes.

coreShorts.q: Differentiate macule from patch.
coreShorts.a: Both are flat, circumscribed, non-palpable areas of discoloration; macule is <1 cm, patch is >1 cm.

coreShorts.q: Differentiate papule from plaque.
coreShorts.a: Both are circumscribed solid palpable lesions; papule is <1 cm and plaque is >1 cm.

coreShorts.q: Give the lecture's examples of papule and plaque.
coreShorts.a: Papule: verruca (wart). Plaque: psoriasis.

coreShorts.q: Describe a nodule.
coreShorts.a: A circumscribed solid skin elevation >1 cm with a deep component involving dermis or subcutis; may extend beneath the surface.

coreShorts.q: Differentiate vesicle from bulla.
coreShorts.a: Both are circumscribed skin elevations containing clear fluid; vesicle <1 cm and bulla >1 cm.

coreShorts.q: What feature distinguishes a cyst from a vesicle/bulla?
coreShorts.a: A cyst has a wall; vesicles and bullae are blisters.

coreShorts.q: Define pustule.
coreShorts.a: A circumscribed skin elevation <1 cm filled with purulent fluid.

coreShorts.q: Define wheal and name its typical skin disease.
coreShorts.a: A transient edematous, erythematous or skin-coloured elevation, variable in size; the primary lesion of urticaria.

coreShorts.q: Contrast open with closed comedo.
coreShorts.a: Open comedo (blackhead) has an open follicular orifice; closed comedo (whitehead) has a closed orifice.

coreShorts.q: Define burrow and name the causative organism stated in the lecture.
coreShorts.a: A linear elevation beneath the stratum corneum produced by the female Sarcoptes scabiei mite; primary lesion of scabies.

coreShorts.q: What makes a lesion secondary?
coreShorts.a: Modification of a primary lesion due to trauma, scratching, oozing, dryness, topical applications or secondary infection.

coreShorts.q: Define crust.
coreShorts.a: Dried serum, blood or pus on the skin surface.

coreShorts.q: Define scale.
coreShorts.a: Accumulated keratin caused by increased proliferation or decreased desquamation of the stratum corneum.

coreShorts.q: Contrast excoriation, fissure and erosion.
coreShorts.a: Excoriation: superficial epidermal discontinuity from scratching; fissure: linear cleft through epidermis into dermis; erosion: partial epithelial loss that heals without a scar.
coreShorts.topic: Secondary tissue loss and chronic changes

coreShorts.q: Define ulcer and its expected healing outcome.
coreShorts.a: Full-thickness epidermal/epithelial loss plus deeper tissue involvement; usually heals with a scar.
coreShorts.topic: Secondary tissue loss and chronic changes

coreShorts.q: Differentiate epidermal from dermal atrophy.
coreShorts.a: Epidermal: thinning of epidermis with wrinkled, shiny appearance. Dermal: loss of collagen or elastic fibres leading to depression.
coreShorts.topic: Secondary tissue loss and chronic changes

coreShorts.q: Define lichenification.
coreShorts.a: Increased epidermal thickness with accentuated natural skin lines, usually from continuous rubbing or itching.
coreShorts.topic: Secondary tissue loss and chronic changes

detailedShorts.q: Summarize why skin examination belongs to the general medical examination.
detailedShorts.a: Skin is the body's largest organ; its colour and lesions may reflect systemic conditions. The lecture specifically includes skin, hair, nails and mucous membranes in the general examination.

detailedShorts.q: Organize the lecture's dermatological clues to systemic disorders.
detailedShorts.a: Pallor → anemia; cyanosis → hypoxia (COPD is given as an example); jaundice → hepatitis; vitiligo or alopecia areata → possible thyroid disease; lichen planus → possible hepatitis C.

detailedShorts.q: Describe the epidermal cells and the distinct function of each.
detailedShorts.a: Keratinocytes form the principal epidermal population, produce keratin and secrete cytokines; melanocytes synthesize melanin; Langerhans cells have an important immune function.

detailedShorts.q: Explain the four-layer ordering described in the lecture.
detailedShorts.a: Deep to superficial: basal on basement membrane (proliferation/renewal), prickle/squamous above basal, granular containing keratohyaline granules, and horny/stratum corneum of anucleate dead keratinocytes.

detailedShorts.q: Describe the layers beneath the epidermis.
detailedShorts.a: Dermis is below basement membrane, with collagen, elastic fibres, glycosaminoglycan matrix and vessels, nerves, follicles and glands. Hypodermis is fat lobules separated by fibrous septa with collagen and large vessels.

detailedShorts.q: Compare eccrine and apocrine gland anatomy without adding external physiology.
detailedShorts.a: Eccrine glands open through sweat ducts onto the epidermal surface widely. Apocrine glands empty into pilosebaceous ducts and occur in flexures, areolae, genitalia and eyelids.

detailedShorts.q: Give two consequences of structural skin changes cited by the lecture.
detailedShorts.a: Absence of hair follicles manifests as alopecia; destruction of melanocytes as depigmentation.

detailedShorts.q: Enumerate the skin functions exactly as listed in the lecture.
detailedShorts.a: (1) Protection from physical/thermal injury, microorganisms and UV; (2) prevent water/electrolyte loss; (3) sweat excretion; (4) temperature control; (5) sensation; (6) vitamin D formation; (7) immunological function; (8) psychological expression and communication.

detailedShorts.q: Which surface and size features distinguish macule, patch, papule and plaque?
detailedShorts.a: Macule and patch: flat/non-palpable discoloration; <1 cm and >1 cm respectively. Papule and plaque: solid palpable lesions; <1 cm and >1 cm respectively. Examples: verruca for papule, psoriasis for plaque.

detailedShorts.q: Compare deep solid and fluid-filled lesions, including the wall distinction.
detailedShorts.a: Nodule is a solid elevation >1 cm with deep dermal/subcutis component. Vesicle and bulla contain clear fluid (<1 cm vs >1 cm). A cyst has a wall and is different from the blisters.

detailedShorts.q: Classify pustule, wheal and comedo according to the source.
detailedShorts.a: Pustule is an elevation <1 cm with purulent fluid; wheal is a transient edematous elevation of variable size and is primary in urticaria; comedo is primary in acne and may be open/blackhead or closed/whitehead.

detailedShorts.q: Explain the appearance and location of a scabies burrow.
detailedShorts.a: Linear elevation under the stratum corneum dug by the female Sarcoptes scabiei mite; a primary skin lesion.

detailedShorts.q: List triggers of secondary lesions and explain the special role of pustules.
detailedShorts.a: Secondary lesions follow changes to primary lesions from trauma, scratching, oozing, dryness, topical applications or secondary infection. Pustules may also occur secondarily from infection in diseases such as scabies or pediculosis capitis.

detailedShorts.q: Differentiate scale and crust by their material.
detailedShorts.a: Scale consists of accumulated stratum-corneum keratin, linked to increased proliferation or decreased desquamation. Crust is dried serum, blood or pus at the surface.

detailedShorts.q: Distinguish excoriation, fissure and erosion according to tissue level.
detailedShorts.a: Excoriation is superficial discontinuity due to scratching; fissure is a linear cleft extending through epidermis into dermis and often painful; erosion is partial epidermal or epithelial loss that does not reach deeper layers and heals without scar.
detailedShorts.topic: Secondary tissue loss and chronic changes

detailedShorts.q: Compare erosion and ulcer with respect to depth and scar.
detailedShorts.a: Erosion remains partial/superficial and heals without a scar (p.9). Ulcer involves full-thickness epithelial loss and a portion of deeper layers, usually healing with a scar (p.10).
detailedShorts.topic: Secondary tissue loss and chronic changes

detailedShorts.q: Compare epidermal atrophy and dermal atrophy using the lecture's descriptions.
detailedShorts.a: Epidermal atrophy: thinning of epidermis gives wrinkling and shiny appearance. Dermal atrophy: collagen/elastic fibre loss yields depression.
detailedShorts.topic: Secondary tissue loss and chronic changes

detailedShorts.a: Scale is accumulation of keratin in the stratum corneum; lichenification is increased epidermal thickness with accentuated natural skin lines following continuous rubbing/itching.
detailedShorts.topic: Secondary tissue loss and chronic changes

detailedShorts.q: How can the shapes and colours of papules and plaques vary?
detailedShorts.a: Papules may be rounded, polygonal, dome-shaped, flattened or pointed; may be skin-coloured, erythematous or violaceous and scaly. Plaques may vary in shape, colour and texture, including scales.

explanation.heading: What is Dermatology?
paragraphs: Dermatology هو فرع الطب المختص بتشخيص وعلاج اضطرابات الجلد. المحاضرة بتبدأ بمعلومتين أساسيتين: الجلد هو أكبر عضو في الجسم، ويمثّل تقريبًا 1/7 من الوزن الكلي للجسم طبقًا للنص، ومساحته في البالغ المتوسط 1.75 m².
الجلد مش مجرد طبقة خارجية: النص يذكر شعر وأظافر وغدد وتراكيب إحساس متخصصة. وعشان كده الفحص العام يشمل Skin وHair وNails وMucous membranes.

explanation.heading: Skin clues to systemic disease
paragraphs: الفكرة هنا إن شكل الجلد أو لونه ممكن يشير لمشكلة عامة: Pallor يرتبط بـAnemia، وCyanosis يرتبط بـHypoxia (ومذكور COPD كمثال)، وJaundice يرتبط بـHepatitis.
كمان المحاضرة بتربط Vitiligo وAlopecia areata بإمكانية وجود Thyroid disease، وبتذكر Lichen planus كعلامة جلدية ممكن ترتبط بـHepatitis C. دي Associations كما وردت بالمحاضرة وليست تشخيصًا منفردًا.

explanation.heading: Epidermis and epidermal cell layers
paragraphs: الجلد في المحاضرة مكوّن من Epidermis وDermis وHypodermis. الـEpidermis هي الطبقة الخارجية ومرتكزة على Basement membrane، وبتضم Keratinocytes وMelanocytes وLangerhans cells.
Keratinocytes هي الخلايا الرئيسية؛ بتكوّن Keratin الذي يساهم في سلامة الجلد وقلة نفاذيته، وبتفرز Cytokines. الـMelanocytes بتصنع Melanin المساهم في لون الجلد، والـLangerhans cells ليها دور مناعي.

احفظ ترتيب طبقات الـEpidermis من تحت لفوق: Basal cell layer (انقسام وتجديد)، ثم Prickle/Squamous cell layer، ثم Granular cell layer (Keratohyaline granules)، ثم Horny cell layer/Stratum corneum (ميتة وبدون أنوية).
understandingAids: ببساطة: أعمق طبقة هي طبقة التجديد، وأسطح طبقة هي الخلايا القرنية الميتة؛ ده تلخيص للترتيب المذكور، مش معلومة امتحانية إضافية.

explanation.heading: Dermis and Hypodermis
paragraphs: الـDermis موجودة تحت Basement membrane، وتتكوّن من Collagen fibres وElastic fibres داخل Matrix of glycosaminoglycans، ومعاهم أوعية دموية ولمفاوية وأعصاب ونهايات عصبية وبصيلات الشعر والغدد الدهنية والعرقية.
الـHypodermis أو Subcutaneous tissue عبارة عن Fat-cell lobules تفصلها Fibrous septa تتكوّن من Collagen ومعاها أوعية دموية كبيرة. فرق مكان الطبقتين وتركيبهما مهم في فهم المصطلحات اللي بعد كده.

explanation.heading: Skin appendages and why structure matters
paragraphs: الـNails تحتوي Hard keratin، والـHair follicles تنتج Hair shafts من Hard keratin.
Sebaceous glands بتفرغ Sebum في Hair follicles بفعل Arrector pili muscles وبتكوّن مع بصيلات الشعر Pilosebaceous units.
Eccrine sweat glands بتفتح على Epidermal surface عن طريق Sweat ducts، بينما Apocrine glands بتفتح في Pilosebaceous ducts، وموجودة في Flexures وAreolae وGenitalia وEyelids.
المحاضرة بتستخدم مثالين يربطوا التركيب بالمظهر: غياب بصيلات الشعر يظهر كـAlopecia، وتدمير Melanocytes يظهر كـDepigmentation.

explanation.heading: Eight functions of skin
paragraphs: المحاضرة بتعدد 8 وظائف: (1) حماية من Physical/Thermal injuries وMicroorganisms وUV، (2) منع فقد الماء والكهارل، (3) إخراج Sweat، (4) تنظيم الحرارة بـVasodilatation وVasoconstriction وSweat evaporation.

وبتكمّل: (5) الإحساس بـTemperature وPain وPressure وTouch، (6) تكوين Vitamin D من Precursor بفعل UVB، (7) وظيفة مناعية تشارك فيها Dendritic cells وKeratinocytes وLymphocytes، (8) وظيفة نفسية في التعبير والتواصل.

explanation.heading: Primary lesions: macule, patch, papule, plaque
paragraphs: Primary lesions هي العلامات الأولى في الأمراض الجلدية. أهم طريقة للتمييز هنا: هل الآفة Flat وغير محسوسة، ولا Solid وPalpable؟ وبعدها نقيس القطر.

Macule وPatch الاتنين Flat, circumscribed, non-palpable areas of discoloration؛ الـMacule أقل من 1 cm، والـPatch أكثر من 1 cm (صفحة 4). ممكن يكون اللون Hypopigmented أوHyperpigmented أوRed أوغيره؛ النص يذكر Pityriasis versicolor وVitiligo كأمثلة.

Papule وPlaque الاتنين Solid palpable lesions؛ الـPapule أقل من 1 cm ومثالها Verruca (wart)، والـPlaque أكثر من 1 cm ومثالها Psoriasis (صفحة 5). الـPapule ممكن تكون بأشكال وألوان مختلفة وقد تغطيها Scales.
understandingAids: لو لون فقط وسطح مسطح فكر Macule/Patch؛ لو كتلة صلبة ملموسة فكر Papule/Plaque. طبّق حد 1 cm كما كتبته المحاضرة، ولا تستنتج تصنيف حالة قطرها 1 cm بالضبط لأن النص ذكر أقل أو أكثر فقط.

explanation.heading: Primary lesions: nodule, vesicle, bulla and cyst
paragraphs: Nodule هي Circumscribed solid elevation أكبر من 1 cm ولها Deep component داخل Dermis أوSubcutis، وممكن تكون كتلتها الأكبر تحت السطح؛ والمثال المكتوب Lepromatous leprosy.
Vesicle وBulla عبارة عن Elevations تحتوي Clear fluid: الـVesicle أقل من 1 cm ومثالها Herpes simplex، والـBulla أكثر من 1 cm ومثالها Bullous impetigo.
الاتنين معًا اسمهم Blisters. المحاضرة تفرّق Cyst عن Vesicle/Bulla بوجود Wall في الـCyst.

explanation.heading: Pustule, wheal and comedo
paragraphs: Pustule هي Circumscribed elevation أقل من 1 cm ومليانة Purulent fluid؛ والمثال المدرج Pustular psoriasis.
Wheal هي Transient, edematous skin elevation، ممكن تكون Erythematous أوSkin-coloured وبأحجام مختلفة؛ دي الـPrimary lesion في Urticaria.
Comedo هي الـPrimary lesion في Acne وعبارة عن Keratinous impaction في Follicular canal. الـOpen comedo = Blackhead وله Open orifice؛ الـClosed comedo = Whitehead وله Closed orifice.

explanation.heading: Burrow and beginning of secondary lesions
paragraphs: Burrow هي Primary lesion في Scabies، وتوصف كـLinear elevation تحت Stratum corneum حفرتها Female Sarcoptes scabiei mite.
بعد كده المحاضرة بتعرّف Secondary lesions بأنها تغيرات في الـPrimary lesions بسبب Trauma أوScratching أوOozing أوDryness أوTopical applications أوSecondary infection.

explanation.heading: Secondary lesions: pustule, crust, scale, excoriation
paragraphs: المحاضرة بتذكر إن الـPustule ممكن تظهر كآفة Secondary نتيجة عدوى ثانوية في أمراض مثل Scabies أوPediculosis capitis، رغم إنها اتذكرت ضمن Primary lesions أيضًا.
Crust هي Dried serum أوBlood أوPus على سطح الجلد (صفحة 8). Scale هي تراكم Keratin بسبب زيادة Proliferation أو نقص Desquamation في Stratum corneum (صفحة 9).
Excoriation معناها Superficial discontinuation of epidermis due to injury، ومذكور Scratching with fingernails كسبب.

explanation.heading: Secondary lesions: fissure, erosion, ulcer, atrophy and lichenification
paragraphs: Fissure هي Linear cleft تعبر Epidermis وتمتد إلى Dermis؛ غالبًا مؤلمة، ومرتبطة في النص بالجفاف الشديد وزيادة سمك الجلد وفقد المرونة.
Erosion هي Partial loss of epidermis/epithelium لا تصل للطبقات الأعمق وHeals without scar. أما Ulcer فهي Full-thickness loss of epidermis/epithelium مع جزء من الطبقات الأعمق وUsually heals with scar.
Atrophy نوعين في النص: Epidermal atrophy بسبب Thinning of epidermis فتظهر Wrinkling/Shiny appearance، وDermal atrophy بسبب Loss of collagen/elastic fibres فتظهر Depression.
Lichenification هي Increased epidermal thickness مع Accentuated natural skin lines نتيجة Continuous rubbing أوItching.
understandingAids: للتثبيت: Erosion سطحية ولا تترك ندبة بحسب النص؛ Ulcer أعمق وعادةً تترك ندبة. الفرق ده مستخرج من صفحتَي 9 و10 فقط.

mcqs.question: What proportion of total body weight does the lecture assign to skin?
mcqs.rationale: The introduction explicitly states 1/7 of total body weight.

mcqs.question: Which examination component is expressly included with skin and hair?
mcqs.rationale: The source lists skin, hair, nails and mucous membranes.

mcqs.question: Which systemic association is paired with lichen planus?
mcqs.rationale: Lichen planus and hepatitis C are linked on p.1.

mcqs.question: Alopecia areata and vitiligo may be associated with which systemic disorder?
mcqs.rationale: The source specifically notes association with thyroid disease.

mcqs.question: Which epidermal layer rests on basement membrane and actively proliferates?
mcqs.rationale: Basal layer rests on basement membrane and renews epidermis.

mcqs.question: Which layer contains keratohyaline granules?
mcqs.rationale: The granular layer contains keratohyaline granules.

mcqs.question: Which cells synthesize the skin's colour contributor melanin?
mcqs.rationale: Melanocytes synthesize melanin, as stated in p.2.

mcqs.question: Which sweat gland opens directly onto the epidermal surface through sweat ducts?
mcqs.rationale: Eccrine glands open on the epidermal surface; apocrine drains into pilosebaceous ducts.

mcqs.question: Which structure is described as fat lobules separated by fibrous septa?
mcqs.rationale: Hypodermis is the subcutaneous fat-lobule layer.

mcqs.question: Which mechanism is listed for skin temperature regulation?
mcqs.rationale: Temperature regulation via vasodilatation, vasoconstriction and sweat evaporation.

mcqs.question: A flat non-palpable 0.5 cm area of skin discoloration is a:
mcqs.rationale: Macule is flat/non-palpable and less than 1 cm.

mcqs.question: A 2 cm circumscribed, solid and palpable skin lesion is termed:
mcqs.rationale: Plaque is a solid palpable lesion greater than 1 cm.

mcqs.question: Which lesion is more than 1 cm, solid, and has a deep dermal or subcutaneous component?
mcqs.rationale: Nodule is a >1 cm solid lesion with deep component.

mcqs.question: A circumscribed blister of clear fluid measuring 0.6 cm is a:
mcqs.rationale: Vesicle <1 cm with clear fluid; a cyst has a wall.

mcqs.question: Which feature differentiates a cyst from vesicles and bullae in the lecture?
mcqs.rationale: The source explicitly mentions a cyst wall.

mcqs.question: The primary skin lesion in urticaria is:
mcqs.rationale: Wheal is listed as the primary lesion of urticaria.

mcqs.question: An open comedo corresponds to a:
mcqs.rationale: Open comedo is a blackhead with an open orifice.

mcqs.question: A linear elevation under stratum corneum dug by female Sarcoptes scabiei is a:
mcqs.rationale: This is the source's definition of burrow, primary lesion of scabies.

mcqs.question: What is a crust composed of?
mcqs.rationale: Crust is dried serum, blood or pus on skin surface.

mcqs.question: Which lesion results from keratin accumulation in stratum corneum?
mcqs.rationale: The source attributes scale to accumulated keratin.

mcqs.question: Which lesion involves a cleft through epidermis into dermis?
mcqs.rationale: Fissure is a linear cleft extending into the dermis.

mcqs.question: Which lesion heals without scar according to the source?
mcqs.rationale: Erosion is partial epithelial loss and heals without a scar.

mcqs.question: Which lesion usually heals with a scar?
mcqs.rationale: Ulcer is full-thickness loss with deeper involvement, usually scarring.

mcqs.question: Accentuation of natural skin lines due to continuous rubbing is:
mcqs.rationale: Lichenification follows increased epidermal thickness from rubbing or itching.

mcqs.question: Loss of collagen/elastic fibres causing depression is:
mcqs.rationale: Dermal atrophy is associated with collagen/elastic fibre loss and depression.
